lessonRef.title: Skill consolidation: creating linear, quadratic, rational, and exponential equations in one variable

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A model gives a required side length of −6 metres. How should this solution be interpreted?
choices: Add 6 to every measurement to correct the model.
Reject the solution; a length cannot be negative, so it lies outside the model’s domain.
Report −6 metres, because the algebra is correct.
Use 6 metres, taking the absolute value.

items.prompt: A repair service charges a $125 call-out fee plus $9 per hour. A job cost $170 in total. Which equation determines the number of hours h?
The formula A = -4bh − 4 models a design constraint, where A, b, and h are positive. Solve it for h.
Item A costs $5 each and item B costs $15 each. You may spend at most $250 in total. Which inequality expresses this constraint on the counts a and b?
A tank holds 110 litres and is filling at 6 litres per minute. After how many minutes does it hold 200 litres?
A model gives the number of buses needed as 4.3. How should this solution be interpreted?
choices: Round down to 4, because 4.3 is closer to 4.
The model must be wrong, because the answer is not a whole number.
Round up to 5; a fractional bus is not viable and rounding down leaves people behind.
Report 4.3, because the model is exact.

items.prompt: A repair service charges a $300 call-out fee plus $3 per hour. A job cost $309 in total. Which equation determines the number of hours h?
The formula A = 2bh + 2 models a design constraint, where A, b, and h are positive. Solve it for h.
Item A costs $8 each and item B costs $9 each. You may spend at most $140 in total. Which inequality expresses this constraint on the counts a and b?

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: A tank holds 45 litres and is filling at 6 litres per minute. After how many minutes does it hold 129 litres?
A budget model allows 12.7 units of a product sold individually. How should this solution be interpreted?
choices: Split the order so the fractional unit is shared.
Round down to 12; buying a partial unit is not possible and 13 would exceed the budget.
Report 12.7, because the constraint is satisfied.
Round up to 13, because 12.7 is closer to 13.
